questions.explaination: A $2 \times 2$ matrix with only one linearly independent eigenvector has geometric multiplicity 1. This implies that the algebraic multiplicity of its eigenvalue must be 2 (repeated eigenvalues, so II is true) and that $P$ is not diagonalizable (so III is true). The determinant may be non-zero (e.g., $\begin{bmatrix} 2 & 1 \\ 0 & 2 \end{bmatrix}$), so I is not necessarily true.

questions.question_text:
Let 𝐴 be any 𝑛× 𝑚 matrix, where 𝑚 > 𝑛. Which of the following statements is/are
TRUE about the system of linear equations 𝐴𝑥= 0 ?

options.A: There exist at least 𝑚−𝑛 linearly independent solutions to this system
options.B:
There exist 𝑚−𝑛 linearly independent vectors such that every solution is a linear
combination of these vectors
options.C: There exists a non-zero solution in which at least 𝑚−𝑛 variables are 0
options.D: There exists a solution in which at least 𝑛 variables are non-zero

questions.explaination: The solution space of the homogeneous system $Ax = 0$ is the null space of $A$, whose dimension is $\text{nullity}(A) = m - \text{rank}(A)$. Since $\text{rank}(A) \le n$, we have $\text{nullity}(A) \ge m - n$. This guarantees the existence of at least $m - n$ linearly independent solutions (A is TRUE). The nullity can exceed $m-n$ when $\text{rank}(A) < n$, so (B) is not universally true.
questions.question_text_latex: Let $A$ be any $n \times m$ matrix, where $m > n$. Which of the following statements is/are TRUE about the system of linear equations $Ax = 0$?

options_latex.A: There exist at least $m-n$ linearly independent solutions to this system
options_latex.B: There exist $m-n$ linearly independent vectors such that every solution is a linear combination of these vectors
options_latex.C: There exists a non-zero solution in which at least $m-n$ variables are 0
options_latex.D: There exists a solution in which at least $n$ variables are non-zero

Let 𝐴 be an 𝑛× 𝑛 matrix over the set of all real numbers ℝ. Let 𝐵 be a matrix
obtained from 𝐴 by swapping two rows. Which of the following statements is/are
TRUE?

options.A: The determinant of 𝐵 is the negative of the determinant of 𝐴
options.B: If 𝐴 is invertible, then 𝐵 is also invertible
options.C: If 𝐴⁡is symmetric, then 𝐵 is also symmetric
options.D:
If the trace of 𝐴 is zero, then the trace of 𝐵⁡is also zero

Organizing Institute: IISc, Bengaluru

questions.explaination: Swapping two rows of a matrix negates the determinant: $\det(B) = -\det(A)$ (A is true). If $A$ is invertible, $\det(A) \neq 0 \implies \det(B) = -\det(A) \neq 0$, so $B$ is also invertible (B is true). Row swapping does not preserve symmetry or trace.

options_latex.D: If the trace of $A$ is zero, then the trace of $B$ is also zero

questions.subtopic: System of linear equations and LU decomposition
questions.explaination: For $PX = Q$ with $P = LU$, solving $LY = Q$ by forward substitution and then $UX = Y$ by backward substitution solves the system. Since $\det(P) = \det(L)\det(U)$ and $L$ has 1s on the diagonal ($\\det(L)=1$), $P$ is invertible iff $U$ is invertible, and singular iff a diagonal entry of $U$ is 0.
